observation_summary: The FastDateFormat class fails to respect the locale provided during instantiation when formatting a Date object, resulting in incorrect week-of-year values. The fix involves passing the locale to the GregorianCalendar constructor.
hypothesis: The FastDateFormat.format(Date) method fails to use the stored locale when creating the GregorianCalendar instance, causing it to default to the system locale's calendar rules (like first day of week), which leads to incorrect week-of-year calculations.
prediction: The source code for FastDateFormat.format(Date) will show 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone)' instead of 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)'.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and fix diff confirm that the locale was missing from the calendar initialization. This is a classic case of incorrect object state initialization.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an initialization error where the object state (the locale) is not correctly applied to the internal calendar used for formatting. This falls under Assignment/Initialization as it involves setting the correct state for the calendar object.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The logic itself is correct; the issue is that the object was initialized with the wrong parameters (missing locale).
